forum.title: STM32F030: Current rises after putting TI CC1125 to SLEEP and entering STANDBY.

forum.content_text:
Cross-posting from [*CC1125 Sleep current rises to ~2mA*](https://e2e.ti.com/support/wireless-connectivity/sub-1-ghz-group/sub-1-ghz/f/sub-1-ghz-forum/1645055/cc1125-cc1125-sleep-current-rises-to-2ma) on the TI forum.

I have a custom board with STM32F030 controlling a TI [CC1125](https://www.ti.com/product/CC1125) sub-GHz radio transceiver via SPI plus a few GPIOs.

Everything is fine for normal operation (TX, RX, etc), but the system has a "Shutdown" mode where the CC1125 is put into its low-power SLEEP state, and the STM32 is in STANDBY.

In SLEEP the CC1125 should take under 1uA but, after sending the SLEEP command, I see the current rise over ~4s and eventually settle at ~2mA.

I have managed to reproduce this using a Nucleo-F030R8 (ST-Link removed) and a TI dev board:

![AndrewNeil_0-1778598375436.png](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/40658db6-1f74-20c5-f96a-d9eec74f9501.png "AndrewNeil_0-1778598375436.png")

The blue line is the total system current (STM32 + cc1125); red line is just the CC1125.

Zooming-in on the Shutdown part:

![ppk2-mpdb-2026-0511-1826-shutdown.png](https://uploads-eu-west-1.insided.com/stmicroelectronics-en/attachment/ba06ddfc-f6ab-9c2e-6657-1fcd25b9232e.png "ppk2-mpdb-2026-0511-1826-shutdown.png")

There seems to be something charging-up and then (partially?) switching-on?

With the CC1125 disconnected, the Nucleo alone takes a steady ~3.1uA with the STM32 in STANDBY.

So it looks like the issue is with the CC1125 somewhere; just posting here in case anyone has any suggestions.

Full details are in the [TI forum post](https://e2e.ti.com/support/wireless-connectivity/sub-1-ghz-group/sub-1-ghz/f/sub-1-ghz-forum/1645055/cc1125-cc1125-sleep-current-rises-to-2ma).
